correctness.rationale: Full if-and-only-if one-long-gap lemma proves domination and induced connectivity for all n≥3,r≥1; exact anchored cyclic compositions yield every coefficient. Sharp maximum total gap length yields minimum, bounded deficits and unique long gap yield multiplicity, and omitted-run counting proves the universal saturation threshold and sharpness. Boundary cases include complete powers and singleton selected sets. Independent adjacency/BFS exhaustive checking of 74,390 subsets across 26 instances agrees with all coefficients; no infinite reasoning rests on that sample.

originality.rationale: The known r=1 connected-cycle polynomial is fully credited. The primary 2024 ordinary domination-polynomial study of powers of cycles does not impose the connected-set restriction; the 2018 connected-polynomial article covers ordinary cycles and other families, and the 2022 homology article offers general interpretations without this evaluation. The exact full polynomial, tight saturation and multiplicity across all r≥2 were not identified in actual research-record, alias and literature comparisons. Priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: Unindexed or differently named cyclic binary-word enumerations may contain an equivalent formula.
Some older scalar results for connected domination of cycle powers and some general algorithmic works were not checked to the last detail.

value.rationale: A natural infinite two-parameter graph family has a complete count of connected dominating sets of every size, resolving an invariant already studied for general graphs and refining ordinary domination results for the same family. The one-long-gap obstruction, rational/logarithmic bivariate series, exact minimum-set multiplicity and sharp universal saturation threshold provide structural and enumerative value beyond scalar parameter substitution. The theorem is meaningful even though the previously known r=1 specialization is explicitly excluded from novelty.
